To play devil's advocate, keep in mind that this is a type of censorship, and Voat has a staunchly anti-censorship stance.

I don't really see this as censorship because they are only banning 'sources' and not the news/material itself. Any news on those websites can be found elsewhere if it was news-worthy, and they don't ban those.

So theoretically, if president Obama bans all mentions of, links to, airwave usage of, and rights to studios for ABC, NBC, BBC, and Al-Jazeera, then says he's not censoring because you can read the news from Fox news, then it's not censorship? I'm not sure I agree.

Your example is not relevant. If a president (dictator in that case) bans all mentions of, links to, airwave usage of, and rights to some media outlets then he's effectively shutting them down. A subverse on Voat doesn't have that power over media sources. Banning them on 1 website on the internet will not stop them for existing.
So, one must shut down an entire source in order to count as censor them? Because that's the measure you're using to define censorship: total silence.

May be I'm not explaining myself well since English is not my first language but the way I see censorship is either like a gag on someone's mouth (so he can't speak at all) or plugs on all his/her listeners ears (so they can't hear what he is saying). Either of these 2 scenarios does not happen when 1 forum decides to ban a certain news source. The news source is still able to publish news and audiences from other websites are able to access their news.
What TIL has done is ban links from certain curator domains. This has nothing to do with the content that they might be publishing. It is not censoring them in any way. You can post links from other sources that publish the same content. The reason for this is that these websites are known for low quality journalism that is based on sensationalism and click-baiting.
